deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is the bottom level (g,n)=(0,3) of the 'Teichmüller tower' of La Longue Marche (1981), enlarged by complex conjugation.

- U = U_{0,3} = P^1_C \ {0,1,∞}.
- Π = Π_{0,3} = π_1(U, b) = <ℓ_0, ℓ_1, ℓ_∞ | ℓ_∞ℓ_1ℓ_0 = 1>, a free group of rank 2. The base point b is written -\vec J, apparently a tangential or symmetric base point.
- Γ = Γ_{0,3} ≅ S_{0,1,∞} × Z/2. It acts on U through the anharmonic group (≅ S_3) together with complex conjugation τ: z ↦ z̄, which commutes with it. This is the extended (orientation-allowing) mapping class group of the thrice-punctured sphere.
- E = E_{0,3} is the extension 1 → Π → E → Γ → 1, i.e. the orbifold fundamental group of [U/Γ]. Dotted letters (ρ̇, σ̇_i) denote elements of Γ; undotted σ_i, ε_i, τ_i are chosen lifts in E.

Programme announced. Π-conjugacy classes of maximal partial splittings (sections of E → Γ over finite subgroups H ⊂ Γ) should correspond to:
- the fixed points in X_{0,3} of the finite-order elements ρ̇ (order 3) and σ̇_0, σ̇_1, σ̇_∞ (the holomorphic involutions);
- '(éventuellement)' the connected components of the fixed loci of the antiholomorphic elements τ, σ_iτ.

This is a discrete/topological analogue, including the real case, of the section conjecture. It is also an orbifold Nielsen-realization statement: torsion in E corresponds to orbifold points of [U/Γ] and to its 'real' strata.

Order-3 points. The fixed points of ρ̇: z ↦ 1/(1−z) are P, P̄ = e^{±iπ/3}. Each has stabilizer of order 6, {1, ρ, ρ², σ_iτ} ≅ S_3, which is the image φ(S_3). The lifts over P̄ are obtained from those over P by conjugating with a lift of any element sending P to P̄. These elements form the coset {σ̇_0, σ̇_1, σ̇_∞, τ, τρ, τρ²}. So one may conjugate by σ_i, ε_i, τ_i, or their products with ρ, ρ².

Isolated holomorphic involutions. σ̇_0: z ↦ z/(z−1) fixes 0 and 2, so its only fixed point in U is 2. The stabilizer of 2 is <σ̇_0, τ> ≅ (Z/2)². The orbit {2, −1, 1/2} has size 12/4 = 3.

Continuation on the next page. Lifting this Klein group into E via a quarter great circle from P to 2 gives σ̇_0 ↦ σ_0, τ ↦ τ_0, and likewise at −1 and 1/2. Then the components of U^τ are the three real arcs, each containing exactly one of 0' = 2, 1' = −1, ∞' = 1/2.

What it serves. The page classifies all conjugacy classes of finite subgroups and partial sections of the extended Teichmüller group at level (0,3), with the tangential/real lifts σ_i, τ_i. These are the building blocks for describing the action of Gal(Q̄/Q) and of complex conjugation on the tower.
errors: Stabilizer of P is written {1, ρ, ρ², σ_1τ, σ_2τ, σ_3τ}; the index should be σ_0τ, σ_1τ, σ_∞τ (indexing slip).

The list 'ρτ, σ_0τ, σ_1τ, σ_∞τ' of elements whose invariant sets give components should contain τ rather than ρτ. ρτ has order 6, and its fixed points would be fixed by both ρ² and τ; no point of U satisfies both, so U^{ρτ} = ∅.

The correspondence between conjugacy classes of maximal partial splittings and fixed points/real components is asserted, not proved here. The hedge '(éventuellement)' shows Grothendieck himself was unsure of the exact formulation in the antiholomorphic case.

ideas.what: Extended Teichmüller group Γ_{0,3} ≅ S_3 × Z/2 (including complex conjugation) and the extension E of Γ by π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞})
ideas.modern_name: extended mapping class group / orbifold fundamental group of [M_{0,4}/S_3 ⋊ conj]; Grothendieck–Teichmüller setting at level (0,3)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Longue Marche 1981, Esquisse 1984); developed by Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981); Esquisse d'un programme §2–3

ideas.what: Conjugacy classes of sections over finite subgroups ↔ fixed points of finite automorphisms and components of fixed loci of antiholomorphic involutions
ideas.modern_name: orbifold Nielsen realization / discrete (topological, real) analogue of the section conjecture; torsion conjugacy classes in mapping class groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kerckhoff (Nielsen realization 1983); real section conjecture: Mochizuki, Pop–Wickelgren, Wickelgren; Galois action on special loci: Collas, Collas–Maugeais
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (discussion of finite subgroups of Teichmüller groups); Longue Marche; letter to Faltings 1983 (real section conjecture)

ideas.what: Explicit computation: ρ-fixed points e^{±iπ/3} with stabilizer S_3; σ_i fixed points 2, −1, 1/2 with stabilizers (Z/2)²; transport between P and P̄ via σ_i or τρ^k
ideas.modern_name: orbifold points of the S_3-quotient of the λ-line (j = 0 and j = 1728 points) with real structure

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out a systematic dictionary between Π-conjugacy classes of maximal partial splittings of E → Γ and fixed points / real components, including the antiholomorphic case (τ and σ_iτ). He then explicitly assigns lifts (σ_i, τ_i) via tangential paths along great circles. A full treatment of this real/antiholomorphic version for higher Γ_{g,n}, with Galois action, is only partially present in later literature.
missed.quote: Les classes de conjugaison de scindages partiels maximaux correspondant aux points fixes de ρ, σ_0, σ_1, σ_∞ opérant sur X_{0,3}, et (éventuellement) aux composantes connexes des ens. d'invariants de ρτ, σ_0τ, σ_1τ, σ_∞τ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Connects to work on torsion and special loci in GT theory (Collas–Maugeais) and to the real section conjecture; including complex conjugation in the Teichmüller tower is less systematically treated.

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful working computations at level (0,3), consistent with La Longue Marche and Esquisse. The real/antiholomorphic partial splittings are a mildly interesting detail but the ideas are largely documented.
transcription_corrections: Dots are dropped throughout: the image shows ρ̇, σ̇_0, σ̇_1, σ̇_∞ (elements of Γ) as opposed to undotted lifts in E.
Stabilizer list in the image reads '1, ρ̇, ρ̇², σ̇_1τ, σ̇_2τ, σ̇_3τ'.
'ℓ_∞ ℓ_1 ℓ_0 = 1' confirmed; the base point is written like '−\vec J' (likely a tangential base point), uncertain.
'Γ envoyant P sur P̄ (à savoir σ̇_0, σ̇_1, σ̇_∞, τ, τρ̇, τρ̇²)'.
